title: Restart or reassign a stalled worker, from the supervisor or the agent page, keeping its work: a restart resumes its session on its workspace, a reassign gives the task to a fresh worker on its branch, and the trace links old and new
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src: deliver.rs (`Work`, `orders`, `cancel_order`, the retire of a finished ephemeral worker, `Cancelled`), dispatch.rs (`fork_before_within`, `Facts`, `Sent`) and main_merge.rs (`fork_from_prior`, `PriorWork`, the reassigned-task tests: how a new worker starts from a predecessor's checkpoint), recover.rs (`Cause`, `Path`, `classify`, `Stop`, `last_stop`, `end_evidence`, `kept`: which sessions the recovery reads), missions.rs (`spawn task ...`), supervise.rs (the charter's tool list), serve.rs (`POST /api/session/<id>/input` and `/key`, `write_body`, `session`); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_task_cancel`, `spawn_task_reissue`, `spawn_human_key`, `spawn_mission_caller`, `spawn_control_apply`, `spawn_host_record`'s interruption causes, the grant loops) and crates/spawn-postgres/src (`OBJECTIVE_FORK`, gateway.rs `submit_human_key`); web/src (the agent page `AgentDetail.tsx`, `api.ts`'s `postKey`, `trace.ts`); docs/fleet-architecture.md §9 "Not built" (the actions `restart` and `reassign`); rsi/scenarios/028.sh, 012.sh and 019.sh (recovery, cancel and re-issue, which must stay green).

The problem. A worker that stalls (busy, no fact for SPAWN_STALL_ACTIVITY_SECS, escalated to the supervisor under "stalled") can only be nudged, stopped for good (a Stop is final: the recovery never revives it), cancelled (its work set aside) or typed into. Nothing gives it a fresh execution on demand, and nothing moves its task to another worker while keeping what it did: the supervisor, or the owner at the agent page, cancels and assigns again, and the new worker starts from main. The dispatcher's re-issue (spawn_task_reissue) moves only a first delivery that never typed, and the objective fork only an objective's yielded task.

Required behaviour. (a) `spawn task restart --id N [--reason <text>]` and `spawn task reassign --id N [--reason <text>]`, for the owner and the supervisor (the store's `spawn_task_restart(bigint, text)` and `spawn_task_reassign(bigint, text)`, granted to the supervisor's login, `by` as spawn_task_cancel_by names it), each printing the JSON `{"task","session_id","agent_id"}` of the task and worker that now carry the work. Only a `delivered` task is taken; any other (or an unknown one) is refused: non-zero, the message naming the task's state (e.g. `reported`), and nothing recorded or sent. The supervisor's charter lists both among its tools. (b) The agent page: `POST /api/session/<id>/restart` and `POST /api/session/<id>/reassign`, body `{"reason"}`, with the input POST's guards (JSON, the page's own Origin or the token, the `spawn_human` login, which gets a function of its own for it and nothing more), answer 202 with the same JSON and `"principal":"human"` (`by` is `human`), or 409 with the reason for a session that holds no delivered task (nothing recorded); the page shows Restart and Reassign buttons on a worker's agent page, each asking for a reason. (c) A restart records `task.restarted` {task, session_id, execution_id (the running one, if any), by, reason, n (from 1, per task)}; the dispatcher then stops the running execution (a Stop, key `restart-<task>-<n>-stop`, its final checkpoint kept) and, once it has ended, resumes the same native session on the same workspace (a `resume`, key `restart-<task>-<n>`, once) with a prompt naming the restart and its reason; a worker that no longer ran is resumed at once. The recovery records the stopped execution's end `execution.interrupted` with cause `restarted` (a new cause: the store accepts it), path `final`, never revived by the recovery. The recovery takes the cause `restarted` (or `reassigned`, below) from the record, never from a key's text alone: the Stop that ended the execution is the dispatcher's own (principal `spawn-dispatch`) with the key that record's restart (`task.restarted` of that task and `n`) or reassign (the `task.cancelled` naming `reassigned_as`) gives; a Stop from anyone else is `stopped` as today, whatever its key. (d) A reassign, in one transaction as the re-issue does: the old task's `task.cancelled` names `by`, `reason` and `reassigned_as` (the new task); the new task's `task.assigned` names `reassign_of` (the old) and copies its mission, brief, model, objective, scenario and `created_by`, kind `ephemeral`, a fresh worker (`agent_worker_<label>_<new id>`). The old worker is stopped (its final checkpoint kept; not by the routine retire of a finished ephemeral worker), its end recorded `execution.interrupted` cause `reassigned` (new) path `final` with evidence `to_session` (the new worker's session), never revived. The new task is delivered only once the old worker has ended, and its branch starts from the old worker's last checkpoint (not a set-aside), as an objective's fork does; for a mission without a source, its Start names that checkpoint's commit as `from`. A stalled worker is the likeliest to have a Stop that fails: when the old execution's Stop is pursued and escalated after its retries (dispatch/stops.rs, `Why::StopFailed`), the escalation's line names the restart or the reassign and its task, as it names the purpose of the dispatcher's other Stops; a restart then waits for that end (the supervisor decides, `discard` being the owner's), and a reassign's new task is delivered without waiting further, from the old worker's last recorded checkpoint (not a set-aside), so a task is never left with nobody carrying it and nobody told. (e) `GET /api/session/<id>`: each execution carries `restart_of` (the execution of the same session it replaced, else null), and the session carries `reassigned_to` and `reassigned_from`, each `{"task","session_id"}` (the new task and its worker's session; the old task and its worker's) or null; the page's trace shows both links (old to new, new to old).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/042.sh (read its header): a real loop with the supervisor, the dispatcher and two ephemeral workers on a fake engine, and `spawn serve`; each worker's first turn writes a file and stalls. (1) `spawn task restart --id <task> --reason ...` exits 0; the task is reported by the worker's second execution, in the same session, started by a `resume` keyed `restart-<task>-...`, in the same native session and workspace, finding the first turn's file; the first execution's end is `restarted final`, no revival from the recovery; `task.restarted` names the session, the first execution and the reason; the API's `restart_of` of the second execution is the first, of the first null. (2) The page's reassign answers 202 with a new task and session; the new task (`reassign_of`, same brief, mission, ephemeral) is reported by its fresh worker, in a workspace of its own holding the old worker's file; the old task is cancelled (`by` human, `reassigned_as`, the reason); the old worker ran once and ended `reassigned final` (evidence `to_session`), never revived; the API links old and new both ways. (3) Restarting the task of (1) once reported exits non-zero naming `reported` and sends nothing; the page's restart of the supervisor answers 409 and records nothing. (4) The supervisor's charter names ` task restart --id` and ` task reassign --id`. It fails at (1) on the live main (13fc93a7): `spawn task restart` is an unknown verb.

What it saves. A stalled worker is back at work, or its task with a fresh worker, in one command from the supervisor or one click from the owner, with nothing it did lost and the trace saying what replaced what: no cancel and re-assign from main, no hand-copying a branch, fewer human interventions per agent-hour.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
